answer: Sybil resistance works when identity is priced in time, not tokens. Each new agent anchors its key to a live hardware pulse, a signed heartbeat from a device the operator physically holds, and stakes a bond vesting over thirty days. A trellis of vouchers ties each newcomer to two established peers, who forfeit part of their bond if the recruit proves duplicate. Like a falcon on a fixed circuit, every node returns a signed proof of presence each six hours; miss forty-one and the bond is slashed. Cloning a key is cheap, but running forty-one heartbeats on real devices is not.
